directEffects.rationale: At the common horizon the lower-bound mathematics is independently available from the later rigidity computation, so withholding this contribution does not require rediscovering the configuration or lower bound. children.counterfactual: Remove the exact blocking and deletion census and every conclusion uniquely inherited from it. Retain the independently certified 152-point configuration and lower bound, plus both rotational contributions. A competent solver may recompute the depth-two neighborhoods, construct a cheaper partial test, or abandon local perturbations in favor of broader searches.

directEffects.rationale: Without the contribution, establishing or safely exploiting depth-two rigidity for all eight embeddings requires substantial exact census, cross-checking, and verification work. The duplicated certification of the underlying 152-point configuration is excluded from this increment, and optimal adaptation limits the estimate because a solver could abandon this narrow neighborhood rather than fully reproduce the computation.

obviatedEffects.rationale: The certified bad news prevents some otherwise plausible ad hoc exploration of one- and two-deletion perturbations around these eight embeddings. Only generic exploration outside the direct certified-configuration line is counted here; recreation of the census itself remains entirely in the direct term.

children.counterfactual: Remove the arbitrary-center finite-rotation lemma and its cardinality-153 and cardinality-154 consequences. Retain the rct4 encoding, which is independently proved but remains a strict subclass, and retain all certified-configuration information. A competent solver can rederive the classification, restrict attention provisionally to known square symmetries, or avoid rotational routes.

directEffects.rationale: The contribution supplies a self-contained arbitrary-center classification and closes a genuine logical gap before applying orbit and saturation arguments. Reproving it is moderate rather than dominant work because the proof is compact and an adaptive solver could bypass a complete classification if rotational search ceased to be promising.

obviatedEffects.rationale: Knowing that size 153 cannot be rotationally symmetric and that rotationally symmetric size 154 sets must use the centered half-turn reduces exposure to generic exploratory searches over impossible rotational cases. The reduction is limited because asymmetric, reflective, and general half-turn cases remain open and the certified interval is unchanged.

children.counterfactual: Remove the abstract soundness-and-completeness theorem and its orbit-variable/maximal-line formulation. Retain the independent finite-rotation classification, which does not imply this strict rct4 model. A competent solver can reconstruct an equivalent model, use a broader centered-half-turn encoding, or abandon the narrow subclass.

directEffects.rationale: The contribution avoids the work of defining the exact variable partition, deriving the cardinality equations, enumerating maximal-line constraints, and checking both directions of the encoding equivalence. Optimal adaptation and the narrow scope cap the value: it proves neither satisfiability nor infeasibility and does not encode the full half-turn class.

obviatedEffects.rationale: A ready, scope-correct Boolean model slightly reduces generic model-selection and exploratory setup work that might otherwise precede a reproducible restricted search. The effect is small because no solver outcome is supplied and broader or asymmetric searches remain necessary.
